variants.01-chambre-observation:
Create ONE complete cinematic science-fiction scene for an interactive game: a robotic interrogation and invasive maintenance chamber, oppressive and disturbing, photographed like a serious live-action science-fiction film with convincing practical set design. NOT an illustration, cartoon, toy render, clean product advertisement or generic neon gaming room. A vulnerable artificial humanoid is restrained in a purpose-built robotic torture/maintenance chair. The machine is a subject the player can harm or help, not an aggressive combat enemy. Convey cruelty through restraint hardware, surgical machinery, intimate framing, cold institutional architecture and the robot's exhausted posture. Its face should communicate a trace of awareness and apprehension without becoming a photoreal human face.
This is a scene concept, so include the entire coherent setup: robot, chair, surrounding treatment chamber, supporting machinery, a foreground tool tray, and environmental light. Frame a medium-wide intimate view with the seated robot visible from head through knees and enough environment to establish the room. Robot face, chest and both forearms must remain visible and sharp enough to understand. Never a distant establishing shot where the robot is tiny. Keep perspective natural and human-scale. Main light must reveal the subject even when the room is dark. Deep blacks are allowed in background, not across all interaction targets. Use restrained film grain, material imperfections, carefully controlled contrast, not glossy plastic everywhere.
Gameplay anchors: one obvious chest electrical connector; an accessible open maintenance panel on a forearm with distinct cables and a lodged metallic fragment; a chunky rotary restraint lock at the opposite wrist. Two arms, two legs, coherent mechanical anatomy and tangible separate components. An electrical probe and extraction pliers rest on a tray in the lower foreground, not floating and not hiding the torso. Robot may show previous wear, subtle dark hydraulic residue and exposed tendon-like actuators, but no active action or obscuring smoke/sparks. No humans or player hands. This is the calm, dreadful moment before an interaction. The robot should not already be destroyed or dismembered.
OUTPUT: a single full-frame horizontal 16:9 image, not a moodboard. No typography, branding, readable signage, UI, watermarks, borders or black letterbox bars. No direct imitation of recognizable fictional characters. Treat the following direction as a complete production-design choice, including the robot's shape, room, chair, camera and lighting.
DIRECTION: Institutional observation chamber. Centered almost perfectly symmetrical frontal shot, camera near the seated robot's eyes. Thick off-white acoustic wall panels, dark one-way observation window behind, floor drain below the chair, brushed steel trolley. Slender gunmetal robot with a subtly asymmetrical pale ceramic faceplate, two small recessed optical eyes and segmented jaw hardware, thin expressive hands. Heavy articulated steel restraint chair with aging pale gray padding. Broad cold surgical lamp from overhead front, faint amber machinery lights only. Muted green-gray and bone-white palette. Quiet, clinical, merciless; detailed realistic film production design, no large glowing sci-fi rings.
